subject: URGENT: BlueHarbor - post-upgrade latency & error spike
messages:
From: Jake Porter <j.porter@blueharbor.com>

Cc: Erin Lowe <erin.lowe@blueharbor.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: deployment completed — seeing big p95 spikes and new errors

Laura —

We just started seeing a large regression after last night's model rollout (v4.2 + quant4 profile). Key metrics for our production route:
- p95 latency jumped from ~320ms to ~1.8s over the 03:00–04:00 UTC window
- 500s / internal errors went from ~0.4% to ~3.2%
- Effective throughput dropped ~18% (more queuing)

This started ~2027-08-16T03:35Z and is still ongoing. Our traffic is time-sensitive (payment reconciliation), so this is causing customer-facing delays. We attached a condensed error log and a few request ids for trace (attachment: blueharbor_error_log_20270815.txt).

Can Redwood fall back to the previous profile for our tenant? We were told the rollout was config-scoped, but the impact looks large. Please advise immediately — this is P0 for us.

—Jake
Jake Porter

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: deployment completed — seeing big p95 spikes and new errors

Laura / team — quick update and preliminary root cause.

What I see in the perf traces (attached: perf_trace_v4.2-quant4.pdf):
- v4.2 introduced a new quantization kernel path for 4-bit profiles that reduces memory but defers certain fused-kernel launches for multi-block attention when sequence length > 512.
- For BlueHarbor’s workload we observed frequent long sequences (~800–1200 tokens) which triggers extra kernel launch/skew that wasn't exercised in our lab microbenchmarks. That causes increased tail latency and higher thread context switching, which in turn increases 500-type errors as queues saturate.
- Additionally, the KV-cache scheduling change in the new profile seems to increase peak GPU memory fragmentation for mixed-batch sizes; that explains the throughput drop.

Mitigation options (ordered by time-to-impact):
1) Route override: Pin BlueHarbor to v4.1/quant8 or v4.1/unquantized for their production route. Estimated impact: immediate; ETA < 30 mins to push and validate. Low cross-tenant risk.
2) Canary rollback of the quant4 kernel changes at runtime for customers with long-seq patterns. ETA ~3 hours including safety validation.
3) Conservative kernel patch to optimize multi-block attention launch — medium-term (~2–3 days) and requires regression testing.

I recommend executing option #1 now while we start a canary rollback (#2) to validate the kernel patch. Diego / Rishi, can you run the route pin and confirm once traffic moves? I'll prepare a quick rollback playbook (draft attached).

—Dev
Dev Patel
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Status update — BlueHarbor production impact and mitigation plan

Hi Jake / Erin — quick update from Redwood engineering and next steps.

What happened: our team identified that the new v4.2 + quant4 profile introduces a kernel scheduling path that increases tail latency on long-sequence workloads. That caused the p95 spike and secondary error rate increase you observed.

What we did now:
- We pinned your production route back to v4.1 (quant8) at 2027-08-16T13:12:00Z. Initial metrics show p95 trending down toward baseline; we'll continue monitoring for the next 2 hours.
- We opened a canary rollback for the quant4 kernel change and started validating on internal traffic.

Next steps:
- Engineering will produce a targeted patch for the kernel launch skew; ETA for a tested fix is 48–72 hours.
- We're preparing an incident postmortem and will share a draft in 24 hours.
- We'll propose a one-time account credit for the impacted window; I'll follow up with your billing lead.

Please expect 15-minute cadence updates until we close. I have looped in our runtime leads (Dev, Markus) and Diego from operations. Deep apologies for the disruption — we understand the urgency and are treating this as P0.

Attachments: rollback_playbook_draft.md (internal), perf_trace_v4.2-quant4.pdf (engineer traces), blueharbor_error_log_20270815.txt (customer-supplied)

Thanks for the patience,
